blocks.text: If you only do one walk while you're in Bondi, make it this one. The Bondi to Bronte coastal walk is a short, cliff-hugging stretch - roughly 2.5km one way - that most people knock over in 45 minutes to an hour, and it's the single best way I know to understand why we live here. You'll pass three beaches, an ocean pool or two, sandstone headlands and more ocean than your camera can hold. It's free, open year-round, and you don't need to be a hiker to do it.

items.label: Time
items.value: 45 min–1 hr at a gentle pace

blocks.text: The route, from my front door to Bronte

The walk kicks off at the southern end of Bondi Beach. Head up Notts Avenue past Bondi Icebergs and you'll find the paved path curling around the cliff - from there it's almost impossible to get lost, because the ocean is on one side the whole way.

First you round Mackenzies Point, the rocky headland with the best wide-angle view back over Bondi - the postcard shot everyone stops for. Every few years, when the sand shifts just right, a fleeting little beach appears at Mackenzies Bay; never guaranteed, but a treat when it shows up.

Next comes Tamarama, affectionately known as 'Glamarama' - a tiny cove tucked between the cliffs. Then it's a short stroll through Bronte Park, under the Norfolk pines, down to Bronte Beach. Bronte feels smaller and more local than Bondi, with an ocean-fed pool at the southern end and cafés across the road made for a post-walk breakfast.

blocks.text: When to go (and how to beat the crowds)

My honest answer: early. Sunrise over the Pacific from Mackenzies Point is worth setting an alarm for, and before about 8am the path is quiet and the light soft and golden. Late afternoon is the runner-up, and weekday mornings are calmer than weekends, when the path fills with joggers, prams and tour groups.

Between roughly May and November you've got a decent chance of spotting humpback whales migrating offshore - scan the horizon from the headlands for a spout or a breach. And in spring, the walk hosts a big free outdoor sculpture exhibition (more below).

blocks.title: Sculpture by the Sea
blocks.text: Each spring the Bondi to Tamarama stretch hosts Sculpture by the Sea - a free open-air exhibition of artworks along the cliffs. Dates shift each year, so check sculpturebythesea.com for this year's exact dates and expect big crowds while it's on.

Do the walk in reverse - Bronte to Bondi - and you'll finish at Bondi with its [bigger choice of cafés](/bondi-eat-and-drink/best-cafes-bondi-beach) and afternoon swims, facing the better views the whole way. Same path, half the crowds coming at you.
What to bring, and swimming along the way

There's very little shade on the cliffs, so treat this as proper sun exposure even in cooler months. Trainers or sturdy sandals are plenty, and there are public toilets and water fountains at both Bondi and Bronte.

items: Sunscreen, hat and water - the path is exposed and there's little shade
Swimmers and a towel if you fancy a dip at Tamarama, Bronte or the ocean pools
Comfortable shoes - sealed path, but with stairs and a few climbs
A camera or phone for Mackenzies Point and the Icebergs pool shot
Cash or card for a café stop at the Bronte end

blocks.title: Swim between the flags
blocks.text: If you swim, only do it at a patrolled beach between the red-and-yellow flags, and check conditions first - this coast has strong rips and the ocean pools can be closed or hazardous in big swell. When in doubt, stay out and enjoy the view instead.

Keen to keep going? Bronte is only the halfway mark of the famous Bondi to Coogee walk, which continues past Waverley Cemetery, Clovelly and Gordons Bay. But even if you turn around at Bronte, you'll have seen the best of it.

items.q: How long does the Bondi to Bronte walk take?
items.a: Most people take about 45 minutes to an hour one way at a relaxed pace over roughly 2.5km. Allow longer if you stop for photos, a swim or a coffee along the way.

items.q: Is the Bondi to Bronte walk easy?
items.a: Yes - it's a sealed, well-marked path suitable for most fitness levels, with some stairs and gentle climbs rather than steep hiking. Ordinary walking shoes are fine, though the stairs mean it isn't fully pram or wheelchair accessible.
At the southern end of Bondi Beach. Head up Notts Avenue past Bondi Icebergs to pick up the coastal path. You can walk it either way.

items.q: Can I swim along the way?
items.a: Yes. You'll pass Tamarama and Bronte beaches plus the Bronte ocean pool, plus Bondi Icebergs at the start. Only swim at patrolled beaches between the flags and check conditions, as this coast has strong rips.

items.q: When is the best time to do the walk?
items.a: Early morning for sunrise and quiet paths, or late afternoon for golden light. Weekdays are calmer than weekends. Aim for whale-watching season (roughly May–November) or catch Sculpture by the Sea in spring.

blocks.text: That's the walk in a nutshell - short enough to do before breakfast, beautiful enough to do again the next morning. Lace up, and I'll see you at the Bronte pool.
